card.What will I do: Your first day in the Group GRC Office. Complete onboarding: record your assignment, sign the undertaking and data rules, and submit your completed READ-ME-FIRST file.
card.Why am I doing this: Every GRC job starts with conduct: you handle other people's data and you produce records that auditors rely on. Before you touch any task, the organisation needs proof that you know the rules (BKB-POL-024 Section 6.1) and that your workspace records your work correctly.
What will I learn: Follow the mentee conduct and data rules — synthetic data only, own work, no AI tools for task work — see BKB-POL-024 Section 3.1; BKB-POL-022 Section 7.1
Recognise what a controlled record looks like: hash, UTC time, version, naming convention — see Capture standard — BKB-MEN-101 Section 9
Use the scripted help: the help note (?) on every step, the glossary and the "Report a problem" form — see Guided Model — principle G7
Keep task data only in your platform folders (00_Admin, 01_Inputs, 02_Working, 03_Submission) — see BKB-STD-001 Section 6 — row "Mentee use"; Capture standard — folders

See which areas of the GRC capability this task practises — U3 Culture and conduct; D1 Mandate, leadership and resources; O6 Speak-up channels and investigation — and what your deliverables evidence — see Ref-Capability map (Learn › Reference pages)
card.How to do it: 6 numbered steps, of which 3 are decisions from options (judgement share 50 %). Rules you will use: copy and calculation only (Learn › Rule tables). Assigned by the Cybersecurity Program Manager, who has written the help note (?) on every step. Help is pre-written on the platform (no live chat).
What to read or refer: BKB-POL-024 — Section 3.1 policy statements; Section 6.1 Procedure: Mentee onboarding
BKB-POL-005 — Acceptable Use Policy
BKB-POL-022 — Section 7.1 Guideline: Using generative AI safely (no AI tool is used for task work)
BKB-STD-001 — Section 6 Handling matrix — row "Mentee use"
BKB Group GRC Charter — Section 10 and Section 10.1 Rules of engagement for mentees

Template: Platform forms (ADM-UND, ADM-RULES) and the file READ-ME-FIRST (ONB-RMF) (issued in /M2610-00001/W01/F1.1/01_Inputs). Submit to /M2610-00001/W01/F1.1/03_Submission. A confirmed conduct breach later is an automatic fail (BKB-MEN-101 Section 13.2 gates). The manifest you test here is the same mechanism that makes every later submission auditable. steps.t: Count the files received for each control

steps.t: Decide for each row: For each file, decide Accept or Reject

steps.o: Accept or Reject, with every failed code, recorded for the 42 files of EVP-IDX
steps.help: You decide one value for every row: for each file, decide Accept or Reject. Walk the checklist beside the table for each file: the result fills Accept/Reject and Defect code. steps.o: Gap or No gap decided for the 6 controls of EVP-GAP

steps.t: Read the new events in RRU-EVENTS
steps.w: Open RRU-EVENTS. Read event N1, then the others, and find what a risk statement (rule R06) and a rating (rule R07) are built from.
steps.o: Three questions on RRU-EVENTS answered
steps.help: RRU-EVENTS lists five events: three new risks, N1 to N3, and two changes to rows already in the register, C1 and C2. Each question's answer is a cell of the sheet: click it. A wrong cell turns amber, with a hint.

steps.t: Choose the best risk statement for each new event (R06)
steps.w: For each new-risk event, choose the draft that follows rule R06: each part filled with the right fact, in the frame's order, and the asset as the register names it. The facts are in RRU-EVENTS (Risk Register › New Risk).
steps.o: Best draft checked for N1 to N3
steps.help: Rule R06 (Learn › Rule tables) gives the frame. Read each draft against the event's facts in RRU-EVENTS: is each part the right fact, in its place, and is the asset the one the event names? Check my answers then shows each row's answer and why, before you complete the step.

steps.t: Rate each new risk (R07)
steps.w: For each new risk, score its inherent likelihood, its inherent impact and its residual likelihood with rule R07, from the facts on each line and the scales of BKB-ERM-001 Sections 6.2 and 6.3.
steps.o: Ratings checked for N1 to N3 (9 lines)
steps.help: Rule R07 (Learn › Rule tables): find the descriptor that uses the same words as the fact and write its number; the residual likelihood counts the existing controls marked working. The scales are BKB-ERM-001 Sections 6.2 and 6.3 (Policies › Policy Library). The platform then works out each score and rating. Check my answers then shows each row's answer and why, before you complete the step.

steps.t: Set each new risk's acceptance authority (R36)
steps.w: For each new risk, choose who may accept it: rule R36, on its residual rating. Use R36's table even where the register's other rows show a different value.
steps.o: Acceptance authority checked for the 3 new risks
steps.help: Rule R36 (Learn › Rule tables) is the Charter's delegation table, Section 6.1 (Policies › Policy Library). Check my answers then shows each row's answer and why, before you complete the step.

steps.t: Choose each new risk's ISO/IEC 27001 controls (Ref-Keywords)
steps.w: For each new risk, find the key words of its category in Ref-Keywords (Learn › Reference pages) and choose the Annex A controls of that row.
steps.o: Controls checked for the 3 new risks
steps.help: Ref-Keywords lists key words, the BKB policy that covers them and its Annex A controls. Match the words of the risk's category. Check my answers then shows each row's answer and why, before you complete the step.

steps.t: Set each new risk's decision and due days (R08)
steps.w: Rule R08: compare each new risk's residual score with the appetite and choose its decision. A risk to treat takes the due days of its residual rating (BKB-ERM-001 Section 7).
steps.o: Decision and due checked for the 3 new risks
steps.help: Rule R08 (Learn › Rule tables) gives the appetite and the decision; BKB-ERM-001 Section 7 (Policies › Policy Library) the due days. Check my answers then shows each row's answer and why, before you complete the step.

steps.t: Decide: Event: "Phishing-resistant MFA rolled out to 100 % of staff…
steps.w: DECIDE: Event: "Phishing-resistant MFA rolled out to 100 % of staff" applies to a phishing risk. What changes? Options: A) Residual likelihood  B) Impact  C) Inherent likelihood. Then: Apply events C1 and C2 to the rows named in "Applies to": for each, choose the change it makes. The change log (R22) records it, field by field.
steps.o: Decision T7.1-D5 checked; C1 and C2 applied in the change log
steps.help: A scripted question: Event: "Phishing-resistant MFA rolled out to 100 % of staff" applies to a phishing risk. What changes? Read the three options and choose one. When you click Check my answer you see the best option and why. Then apply events C1 and C2 to the rows named in "Applies to": their facts are in RRU-EVENTS (Risk Register › New Risk). Rule R22 (Change log): One change-log row for each changed field: row ID, field, old value, new value, event ID, evidence.

steps.t: Decide: Which risks go in the "above appetite" part of the note
steps.w: DECIDE: Which risks go in the "above appetite" part of the note? Options: A) Inherent score > 11  B) All High inherent risks  C) Residual score > 11. Then: Complete RR-NOTE: list the risks above appetite, and the rows whose acceptance authority is not the one rule R36 gives. The new and changed risks are listed for you.
steps.o: Decision T7.1-D6 checked; RR-NOTE completed
steps.help: A scripted question: Which risks go in the "above appetite" part of the note? Read the three options and choose one. When you click Check my answer you see the best option and why. Then complete RR-NOTE from the register on Risk Register › Score Risk and your own three rows. BKB-ERM-001 Section 4 (Policies › Policy Library) sets the appetite.

steps.t: Classify each asset by its Ref-Chain asset type

steps.o: Asset type checked for the 3 assets

steps.t: Choose each new risk's treatment option (L12)
steps.w: [LI-03 — Asset–threat–vulnerability–control chain and control attributes] For each new risk, choose its treatment option with rule L12, from its residual score in RR-UPD.
steps.o: Treatment option checked for the 3 risks
steps.help: Rule L12 (Learn › Rule tables) gives the option from the residual score. Check my answers then shows each row's answer and why, before you complete the step. This is a Lead Implementer extension step: it adds to the task, with its own template and deliverable.

steps.t: Copy the Annex A control for each chain's threat (Ref-Chain)

steps.t: Decide: The owner wants to treat a data-breach risk only by buying …
steps.w: [LI-03 — Asset–threat–vulnerability–control chain and control attributes] DECIDE: The owner wants to treat a data-breach risk only by buying cyber insurance. Is the risk treated? steps.o: Decision T7.1-D8 checked; L05 attributes recorded for the 3 controls
opt: Partly — the financial impact is shared, but controls are still needed
steps.help: A scripted question: The owner wants to treat a data-breach risk only by buying cyber insurance. Is the risk treated? Read the three options and choose one. When you click Check my answer you see the best option and why. Then do the step that follows: Apply rule L05 for the three attributes. steps.t: Choose each risk's treatment action

steps.o: Treatment action checked for the 3 risks
steps.help: Read each risk's statement and option, and the facts of its event in RRU-EVENTS (Risk Register › New Risk). steps.t: Link each action to its control (L12)

steps.o: Control checked for the 3 actions
steps.help: Each row offers the controls of its risk's category in Ref-Keywords, with their titles. Check my answers then shows each row's answer and why, before you complete the step. This is a Lead Implementer extension step: it adds to the task, with its own template and deliverable.

steps.t: Set each action's due date (R08)
steps.w: [LI-09 — Risk treatment plan] Each action's owner is the risk's owner in RR-UPD, copied for you. Rule R08 gives the due days of a risk to treat by its residual rating: count them from the plan's date, 2026-11-19, and type the due date. A retained risk has none: type none.
steps.o: Due date checked for the 3 actions
steps.help: Rule R08 (Learn › Rule tables) and BKB-ERM-001 Section 7 (Policies › Policy Library) give the days. Count calendar days. Check my answers then shows each row's answer and why, before you complete the step. This is a Lead Implementer extension step: it adds to the task, with its own template and deliverable.

steps.t: Estimate each risk's residual score after treatment (R07)

steps.o: Expected residual checked for the 3 risks
steps.help: Rule R07 (Learn › Rule tables): a working control lowers the residual likelihood by one; the impact stays. Check my answers then shows each row's answer and why, before you complete the step. This is a Lead Implementer extension step: it adds to the task, with its own template and deliverable.

steps.t: Request approval: who accepts each residual (R36)

card.What will I do: Vulnerability-remediation SLA compliance test. Test vulnerability-remediation SLA compliance (R24) and report it per class. Includes ISO/IEC 27001 Lead Implementer extension(s) LI-11.
card.Why am I doing this: Vulnerability management is where policy meets reality: the policy promises to fix criticals in 7 or 14 days; the scanner shows what actually happened. The Vulnerability Management Governance Analyst measures the gap, validates exceptions and reports compliance per class — numbers management can act on.
What will I learn: Classify findings into policy classes (KEV / internet-facing first) and compute due dates and status — see Rule R24; BKB-POL-010 Section 4; Ref-Test rules

pl.note: Vulnerability scanner export of LearnTech's Amsterdam office on 2026-11-19, the test date: 172 findings first detected in the last six months (dataset VUL-FINDINGS, synthetic). Last scan is the latest scan of the asset, and Found in last scan whether that scan still found the vulnerability. Exception ID points to the exception register.

steps.t: Set the policy class of each kind of finding (R24)
steps.w: VUL-TEST's class rules list each kind of finding in the scanner export, by exposure, KEV listing and scanner severity, with how many findings are of that kind. Choose each kind's policy class with rule R24; the workbook then gives each of the 172 findings its class.
steps.o: Class checked for the 9 kinds of finding
steps.help: Rule R24 (Learn › Rule tables) lists the classes in order: the first that fits the finding gives its class. KEV-listed means the vulnerability is in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue: attackers are already using it. Check my answers then shows each row's answer and why, before you complete the step.

steps.t: Work out the due date of one finding of each class
steps.w: Before relying on the workbook's due-date formula, work out by hand the due date of one finding of each class: first detected + the class's SLA in days (rule R24). Once your four dates are checked, the formula fills the Due column of all 172 findings.
steps.o: Due date checked for four findings, one of each class
steps.help: Rule R24: due = first detected + SLA. Count calendar days, across the end of a month. Check my answers then shows each row's answer and why, before you complete the step.

steps.t: Decide each finding's status at the test date
steps.w: For each of the 172 findings, compare its closed date with its due date, or, if it is still open, the test date (2026-11-19) with its due date, and choose its status.
steps.o: Status checked for the 172 findings
steps.help: A closed finding is in SLA when it was closed on or before its due date; an open finding is in SLA while its due date has not passed at the test date. Use the dates only: whether a fix is verified is step 5, whether an exception holds is step 4. Check my answers then shows each row's answer and why, before you complete the step.

steps.t: Test each exception (R24)
steps.w: For each exception in the register, decide whether it is valid at the test date, 2026-11-19, with rule R24's validity test.
steps.o: Validity checked for the 12 exceptions
steps.help: Rule R24 (Learn › Rule tables), its last sentence, is the validity test: every part of it must hold. Check my answers then shows each row's answer and why, before you complete the step.

steps.t: Check each closure was verified by a re-scan
steps.w: For each closed finding, decide whether its fix was verified as BKB-POL-010 Section 6.1 step 4 requires: read its closed date against the scanner's last scan, and what that scan found.
steps.o: Verification checked for the 98 closed findings
steps.help: BKB-POL-010 (Policies › Policy Library), Section 6.1 step 4, says when a fix counts as verified. Check my answers then shows each row's answer and why, before you complete the step.

steps.t: Work out compliance per class
steps.w: For each class, count the findings within SLA as BKB-POL-010 Section 10 defines it, and type the class's compliance: within SLA / all findings = %, to one decimal.
steps.o: Compliance checked for the 4 classes
steps.help: Section 10 of BKB-POL-010 (Policies › Policy Library) says which findings are within SLA. Under each class, the workbook counts its findings by what steps 3 to 5 found. Check my answers then shows each row's answer and why, before you complete the step.

steps.t: Decide which recommendation comes first
steps.w: DECIDE: If most breaches in a test were class 1 findings on internet-facing assets, which recommendation would come first? Options: A) Patch or isolate internet-facing criticals within 7 days  B) Buy a new scanner  C) Change the SLA to 30 days. Then: Write VUL-MEMO's three recommendations with rule R25: count the breaches of each deviation type of Ref-Actions, V1 to V4, and choose the actions of the three with the most, most first.
steps.o: Decision T8.1-D5 checked; the three recommendations checked
opt: Patch or isolate internet-facing criticals within 7 days
steps.help: A scripted question first: which recommendation comes first when most breaches are class 1 on internet-facing assets. When you click Check my answer you see the best option and why. Then VUL-MEMO's recommendations: rule R25 (Learn › Rule tables) orders them by the number of breaches; the deviation types and their actions are Ref-Actions' V1 to V4 (Learn › Reference pages). steps.t: Read the tracker before testing it

steps.t: Run the four closure tests on each action reported Closed
steps.w: For each action its owner reports Closed, run rule R33's four closure tests in order: evidence attached, dated after raising, a system record, re-test passed. Record Pass if all four pass, Fail at the first that fails.
steps.o: Closure tests checked for every action reported Closed
steps.help: Rule R33 (Learn › Rule tables): an action is verified only if all four tests pass. Read each test against the action's own cells; an empty cell is no evidence. Check my answers then shows each row's answer and why, before you complete the step.

steps.t: Record the reason code of each reopened action
steps.w: Each action that failed a closure test is Open again. Record its status with the code of the test that failed: rule R33's codes K1 to K4.
steps.o: Status and reason code checked for each reopened action
steps.help: R33 (Learn › Rule tables) gives each test a code: K1 evidence attached, K2 dated after raising, K3 a system record, K4 re-test passed. Its tests are read in that order. Check my answers then shows each row's answer and why, before you complete the step.

steps.t: Decide which open actions to escalate
steps.w: For each open action, decide whether it goes to its owner's manager: rule R33, more than 14 days past its due date at the test date, 23 December 2026, and not escalated yet.
steps.o: Escalation checked for every open action
steps.help: Count the days from each action's Due date to 23 December 2026. Its Escalated column says whether it has gone up already. Check my answers then shows each row's answer and why, before you complete the step.

steps.t: Record how many days each open action is past due
steps.w: For each open action, type how many days past its due date it is at the test date, 23 December 2026: 0 where the due date has not passed. Its next check date, the test date + 14 days (rule R33), is written for you.
steps.o: Days past due checked for every open action; next check dates set
steps.help: Count calendar days from the Due date to 23 December 2026. Check my answers then shows each row's answer and why, before you complete the step.

steps.t: Tell each owner what closes a reopened action

steps.o: What each reopened action needs checked; requests to owners written

card.What will I do: Surveillance-audit support — answering auditor requests and a finding. Answer eight auditor requests from EVIDENCE-INDEX and respond to finding NC-1 (R34). Includes ISO/IEC 27001 Lead Implementer extension(s) LI-18.
card.Why am I doing this: At the surveillance audit the certification body asks for evidence and raises findings. The auditee answers each request from the evidence repository and responds to a finding from the evidence: what is sent, and how a finding is answered, is what the auditor concludes from. This is the moment all earlier work is tested.

Respond to a nonconformity: accept with corrective action or challenge with the evidence row — see Rule R34, L25; ISO/IEC 27001 cl. 10.2
Know what happens to a finding still disputed after the audit (LI-18) — see ISO/IEC 17021-1 (appeals)

card.How to do it: 12 numbered steps, of which 6 are decisions from options (judgement share 50 %). Rules you will use: R34, L25 (Learn › Rule tables). Assigned by the Information Security Auditor, who has written the help note (?) on every step. Help is pre-written on the platform (no live chat).

BKB-POL-016 — Section 6.2 External audit coordination
Ref-Rules — R34, L25

R01: Ask in this order and stop at the first "yes": 1) Made by a parliament or a regulator? → Law / regulation. 2) Can an organisation get a certificate? → Certifiable standard. 3) Is the result an auditor's report on controls? → Attestation framework. 4) Is it contract wording? → Model contract. 5) Otherwise → Voluntary framework.
R02: A standard applies to an office when the addendum Section 2 row for that office names it, or the addendum Section 3 says "all offices". Copy the office names. Do not add offices.
R03: Take the three obligations for the office with the shortest deadline in addendum Section 2 (hours before days). If there are fewer than three, add mandatory standards in the order of addendum Section 3.
R04: Copy the first five parties listed in addendum Section 4, in the same order, with the requirement written next to each.
R05: Walk the BKB-STD-001 Section 5 decision tree from Q1. Then apply BKB-POL-004 Section 3.1: personal data, children's data and credentials are never below Tier 3; aggregated data takes the highest tier of its parts; derived outputs take the tier of the source.
R06: Write: "Because of <cause>, <event> may occur, leading to <consequence> for <asset>." Copy the words for cause, event and consequence from the scenario facts. Copy the asset name from the register.
R07: Find the likelihood and impact descriptor in the ERM scale table (BKB-ERM-001 Section 6.2–6.4) that uses the same words as the facts. Write the descriptor number. Residual likelihood = inherent likelihood − 1 for each existing control marked "working" (lowest value 1). Residual impact = inherent impact. Score = likelihood × impact. Rating: 1–5 Low, 6–11 Medium, 12–19 High, 20–25 Critical.
R08: LOW-criticality appetite = 11. Residual score ≤ 11 → Decision "Accept and monitor". Residual score > 11 → Decision "Treat"; due days from BKB-ERM-001 Section 7: Critical 30, High 90, Medium 180.
R09: Check D1 to D10 in order (Ref-Defect codes). If any check fails → Reject and write every failed code. If none fails → Accept. If D9 fails, also click "Report data issue" and do not copy the content.
R10: If a sentence has two actions (joined by "and" or ";"), make two rows. Owner role = the owner of the linked BKB policy in the BKB-POL-000 index.
R11: Full = a BKB policy clause AND a procedure AND an Annex A control exist. Partial = only one or two of the three exist. None = none exists.
R12: Write: "Missing: <policy clause / procedure / control>. Owner: <policy owner>."
R13: Covered = a clause has the same action AND the same time limit. Partly = the action is there but the time limit or owner is missing. Not covered = no clause. Where to fix: requirement names a country or office → Addendum; otherwise → Group policy. Redline frame: "<Role> shall <action> within <time limit>." Never make a Group value weaker; if it would, write "Exception needed".
R14: Use the six fixed steps: 1 Trigger received → 2 Check input → 3 Do the action → 4 Record → 5 Tell the owner → 6 Exception: escalate. For each step copy the responsible role and the time limit from the addendum Section 5 or the policy clause shown on your task page. Do not invent numbers.
R15: Look up the control frequency in Ref-Sampling and copy the minimum sample. Select the sample with the random seed shown on your task page (the platform does the selection when you click "Select sample").
R16: Fieldwork starts 30 days after the end of the audit period. Due date = fieldwork start − 5 working days.
R17: Copy for every request: "The evidence must be dated, show who produced it, cover the whole period and be an unchanged system export."
R18: A control has a gap when it has fewer than 2 accepted files. For each gap write: "Please send 2 more files for <control> covering <period> by <due date>."
R19: Effective: no exceptions. Effective with exceptions: only Low/Medium exceptions and ≤ 5 % of the population. Not effective: any High exception or > 5 %. Control tests (T8.2): 1–2 deviations = effective with exceptions; > 2 = not effective.
R20: Copy the action for the exception type from Ref-Actions (e.g., U1 active leaver account → "Disable within 1 working day; check for use after termination" — owner IAM team).
R21: Voluntary leaver: account disabled within 4 hours of termination. Involuntary leaver: within 1 hour. KPI = leavers fully disabled within SLA ÷ all leavers × 100.
R22: One change-log row for each changed field: row ID, field, old value, new value, event ID, evidence.
R23: Sort by residual score (highest first); for equal scores, higher inherent score first. Trend: score went up ↑, down ↓, no change →. "So what" frame: "If this happens, <consequence copied from the statement>." Risk for acceptance = the Medium risk with the highest residual score (equal scores: lowest Risk ID). Expiry = today + 12 months; re-assessment = expiry − 30 days; approver = rule R36.
R24: Class 1: KEV-listed or Critical on an internet-facing asset → 7 days. Class 2: Critical, or KEV on an internal asset → 14 days. Class 3: High → 30 days. Class 4: Medium → 90 days. Due = first detected + SLA. Exception valid only if approved by system owner AND CISO, has a compensating control, and has not expired.
R25: Write three recommendations: the Ref-Actions action for the three classes (or deviation types) with the most breaches, in that order.
R26: High = affects a Mission Critical system or no evidence exists. Medium = done late or partly. Low = record-keeping only.
R27: Use the tier from rule R35. Then include every question in Ref-Questions marked for that tier or a lower tier. Clause checklist: include every clause marked for the tier; add "transfer mechanism" if data leaves the country.
R28: Check S1–S9 (Ref-SOC checks). Reject if S4 (qualified opinion) or S9 (service not in scope). Otherwise Approve with conditions if any S-check fails (one condition per failed check from Ref-Conditions, due in 90 days). Approve if none fails.
R29: Role = the value in the dataset column "Role (contract register)". DPIA required = Yes if the activity involves any of: children or students, AI/analytics/profiling, monitoring or recording, health data, identity checks (KYC/AML). Otherwise No.
R30: For every affected office and every data-subject country, look up the regimes in addendum Section 2. Deadline = discovery time (UTC) + clock. Mark the earliest firm deadline. Tell data subjects = Yes if the data includes children's data, health data, financial data or credentials, or more than 1,000 people; otherwise No.
R31: Use the 4-week template: Week 1 lesson, Week 2 poster + quiz, Week 3 phishing simulation, Week 4 results + refresher. Copy the scenario card and the 3 behaviours for your theme from Ref-Content. Approvals: HR + Legal always; add works council where addendum Section 2 lists one for the office.
R32: Copy the obligations from the official source (steps in T11.2). Applicability per office: rule R02. Affected policies: use the keyword table in Ref-Keywords. Action due date = publication date + 30 days.
R33: An action is "Closed — verified" only if all are true: closure evidence is attached (else K1); it is dated after the action was raised (else K2); it is a system record, not a statement (else K3); the re-test passed (else K4). Otherwise the status is "Open" with the failed code. An open action more than 14 days past its due date and not yet escalated → escalate to the owner's manager (K5). Next check date = test date + 14 days.
R34: Answer each request with ONE evidence file: same control or clause, dated inside the audit period, from a system (not an undated screenshot). Record file ID and SHA-256. If no file matches, answer "No evidence available" and raise an action (never create evidence after the request). For a finding: open the named evidence file — if it shows the problem, accept and state the corrective action; if it shows the control worked, challenge with the row; if still disputed, name the route (closing meeting, then the certification body's appeal process).
R35: Critical: access to Tier 4 data or children's data at scale, OR a customer-facing or regulatory-critical service that is hard to replace. High: access to Tier 3 personal/confidential data at volume, OR a revenue-critical service. Medium: limited personal data or pseudonymous data, easy to replace. Low: only public/anonymous data. Check from Critical down; stop at the first match.
R36: Low → Risk owner. Medium → Org CRCO. High → Org CEO + Group CISO. Critical → Not acceptable (Board decision). Source: Charter Section 6.1. Always use this table, even if the register shows a different value.
L01: Clauses 4, 5, 6, 7 → Plan; clause 8 → Do; clause 9 → Check; clause 10 → Act (conventional mapping).
L02: Requirements = ISO/IEC 27001, ISO/IEC 27006-1, ISO/IEC 17021-1. All other listed documents = guidance.
L03: In scope = the office(s) and departments of your organisation in the asset register. Out of scope = only the items listed as "excluded" in the addendum, with the addendum reason. Interfaces = the first 3 external rows of the TSA Integrations sheet. Climate change relevant = Yes (Group decision, BKB-POL-015); copy the Group reason from the sheet Ref-ISMS processes.
L04: Copy the 10 ISMS processes and owners from Ref-ISMS processes (Learn › Reference) (the Group RACI in the Charter: risk assessment, SoA, document control, competence, awareness, incident, supplier, internal audit, management review, corrective action).
L05: Copy the control type, security property and cybersecurity concept for the control from Ref-27002 attributes (Learn › Reference).
L06: Every control is Applicable. A control is Not applicable only if it appears in Ref-SoA exclusions (Learn › Reference); copy the justification shown there. Justification for applicable controls: copy the first source found in this order — risk register treatment ID, law in addendum Section 2, contract in Organization_Profiles, "Group baseline (BKB-POL-001)".
L07: Look up the control in the TSA Control_Mapping sheet. Product listed → "Yes". Listed in the Roadmap sheet only → "Planned". Not listed → "No".
L08: For each of the 7 items, search BKB-POL-001 for the key word in the template. Found → copy the section number. Not found → "Gap".
L09: Copy the RACI from the Charter table for the 10 ISMS processes (rule L04). Do not change any letter.
L10: Copy the 14 rows from the template; for each, write the BKB library location from Ref-Locations (Learn › Reference).
L11: Copy from Ref-Certification card (Learn › Reference): Stage 1 = documents and readiness; Stage 2 = implementation on site; surveillance in years 2 and 3; recertification before year 3 ends. Certification-body criteria = the 5 listed on the card, in order.
L12: Residual score > 11 → "Modify". Residual score ≤ 11 → "Retain". Controls = the SoA controls listed for the risk category in Ref-Keywords.
L13: For each clause look up your deliverable in Ref-Clause map (Learn › Reference). Deliverable submitted and accepted → "Conforms". Submitted with review comments → "Partial". Not in the list → "Gap".
L14: Copy the 3 objective templates from the sheet Ref-Objectives. Fill the numbers: leavers disabled within 4 h (target 95 %), critical vulnerabilities fixed within SLA (target 90 %), staff trained (target 95 %). Owner and date from the template.
L15: Copy the 6 fixed milestones from the sheet Ref-Milestones (scope approved → SoA approved → controls implemented → internal audit → management review → Stage 1). Start = programme week 12 + 1 month; each milestone lasts 1 month. Owner = RACI "A" for that process.
L16: Copy the 10 field names from the sheet Ref-Measure card. Fill each field from your VUL-TEST (formula, numbers) and the fixed values on that sheet (frequency monthly, analysed by GRC team, evaluated by CISO, reported to management review).
L17: Major = the required activity was never done in the period OR failed in more than half of the sample. Minor = any other failure.
L18: Answer the 5 fixed questions on the form (sheet Ref-5-Whys) by copying facts from your test evidence. The last answer is the root cause. Correction = the Ref-Actions action for the instance. Corrective action = "Add the missing step to the procedure and train the owners". Effectiveness check = re-test 3 months later.
L19: Copy the service model from the vendor intake form. Copy the responsibility table for that model from the sheet Ref-Cloud. Add the 5 fixed cloud and supply-chain questions from the same sheet.

Log storage costs led IT to propose cutting online retention to 90 days.
Cause: online log retention cut to 90 days. What may happen: deletion of security logs before an incident found late is investigated. Consequence: a reportable breach left uninvestigated.
Incidents found more than 90 days after they started: about once a year at the office (incident register, 2023–2026).
A reportable breach the office cannot investigate, and a warning from the National Privacy Commission.
SIEM alerting on live logs (working); monthly log-source coverage review (not working: two reviews missed in 2026)
The customer onboarding team exports data to spreadsheets for manual processing.
Privacy — exposure of customer personal data

Cause: customer data exported to spreadsheets for manual onboarding. What may happen: a spreadsheet of customer personal data sent or saved outside the CRM. Consequence: large-scale personal-data harm to customers.
Spreadsheets of customer data found outside the CRM several times a year (DLP alerts, 2026).
Large-scale personal-data harm: the largest export held 40,000 customer records.

A critical SaaS supplier announces end-of-support for the API version the office uses in 60 days.

Cause: the supplier's end-of-support for the API version the office uses. What may happen: failure of the integration between the supplier's platform and the case workflow. Consequence: customer cases not handled during the outage.
A supplier retires an API the office uses about once a year (ITSM records, 2022–2026).
Outage 24–72h: customer cases not handled while the integration is rebuilt.
Supplier change notices reviewed monthly (working); fallback to manual case entry (not working: never tested)
New KRI data: threshold breached for two consecutive months.

Treatment plan due date passed with 50 % completion.

R-16-HQ-12's treatment action, “Maintain country crisis plan with evacuation and remote-operation options”, was due on 2026-10-31. On that date it was 50 % complete: the crisis plan is drafted, not yet approved or tested. It is not one of the risk's existing controls.

Because the Manila, Philippines office operates 10 Mission Critical and 81 registered assets (e.g., Treasury management system, Banking & payment files) and the Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) & KPO industry faces social-engineering of agents, credential theft and ransomware cascading into client environments, a ransomware attack may encrypt production and backup data, disrupting 'Call handling and customer query resolution' beyond RTO and triggering notification under Data Privacy Act 2012.
EDR; immutable backups (3-2-1-1-0); MFA; network segmentation; IR retainer (HIGH/MEDIUM)
Phishing and business-email compromise leading to credential theft or fraudulent payment

Because staff at Manila, Philippines (Finance & Treasury (Group)) receive targeted phishing and payment-diversion requests, attackers may compromise mailboxes or induce fraudulent payments, causing direct loss and data exposure.
Email security (DMARC p=reject, sandboxing); phishing-resistant MFA; call-back verification for payment changes; awareness
Personal-data breach through misconfigured cloud / SaaS services

Because 15 assets at Manila, Philippines hold personal or regulated data (e.g., HR Information System (HRIS), Payroll system) on 38 SaaS and 31 cloud-hosted services, misconfiguration or excessive access may expose personal data, requiring notification (72h to NPC and data subjects).

Inadequate recovery capability for Mission Critical assets

DR plans; HA architecture; backup testing per band
Data loss through endpoints, remote working and removable media

p: COPC CX Standard An industry performance standard for customer-experience operations, written by COPC Inc. Contact centres can be certified against it.
GDPR / DPA 2012 / KVKK Laws. Breach clocks, lawful basis, rights and transfers.
HIPAA A US federal law (1996), enforced by the HHS Office for Civil Rights. Healthcare providers and their business associates must comply.
ISO 9001 A certifiable quality management-system standard: accredited certification bodies audit organisations and certify them against it.

ISO/IEC 17021-1 Requirements for the certification bodies that audit and certify management systems, ISO/IEC 27001 among them. A certification body must have a documented process to receive, evaluate and decide on appeals against its decisions (clause 9.7), and one for complaints (clause 9.8).
ISO 18295 A certifiable ISO standard for customer contact centres: service requirements a centre can be certified against.
ISO/IEC 27001 A certifiable management-system standard: clauses 4–10 (Plan-Do-Check-Act) plus 93 Annex A controls.

ISO/IEC 27001 documented information Clause 7.5 controls all of it. Where a clause says the organisation shall “maintain” documented information, it is a document: kept current and changed under control, such as a scope, a policy, a process or objectives. Where it says “retain” documented information, as evidence, it is a record: kept unchanged as proof of what was done or found, such as evidence of competence or the results of a review, an audit or a measurement.
NIST CSF 2.0 A voluntary framework: Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover.

PCI DSS A card-data security standard set by the PCI Security Standards Council, founded by the card brands; not a law. It binds merchants and service providers through their contracts with banks and card brands, and compliance is shown by a qualified assessor's Report on Compliance on their controls.
SOC 2 An auditor's report on a service organisation's controls. Type II tests they worked over a period.

r: Ask in this order and stop at the first "yes": 1) Made by a parliament or a regulator? → Law / regulation. 2) Can an organisation get a certificate? → Certifiable standard. 3) Is the result an auditor's report on controls? → Attestation framework. 4) Is it contract wording? → Model contract. 5) Otherwise → Voluntary framework.
A standard applies to an office when the addendum Section 2 row for that office names it, or the addendum Section 3 says "all offices". Copy the office names. Do not add offices.

Take the three obligations for the office with the shortest deadline in addendum Section 2 (hours before days). If there are fewer than three, add mandatory standards in the order of addendum Section 3.
Copy the first five parties listed in addendum Section 4, in the same order, with the requirement written next to each.

Walk the BKB-STD-001 Section 5 decision tree from Q1. Then apply BKB-POL-004 Section 3.1: personal data, children's data and credentials are never below Tier 3; aggregated data takes the highest tier of its parts; derived outputs take the tier of the source.
Write: "Because of <cause>, <event> may occur, leading to <consequence> for <asset>." Copy the words for cause, event and consequence from the scenario facts. Copy the asset name from the register.

Find the likelihood and impact descriptor in the ERM scale table (BKB-ERM-001 Section 6.2–6.4) that uses the same words as the facts. Write the descriptor number. Residual likelihood = inherent likelihood − 1 for each existing control marked "working" (lowest value 1). Residual impact = inherent impact. Score = likelihood × impact. Rating: 1–5 Low, 6–11 Medium, 12–19 High, 20–25 Critical.
LOW-criticality appetite = 11. Residual score ≤ 11 → Decision "Accept and monitor". Residual score > 11 → Decision "Treat"; due days from BKB-ERM-001 Section 7: Critical 30, High 90, Medium 180.
Check D1 to D10 in order (Ref-Defect codes). If any check fails → Reject and write every failed code. If none fails → Accept. If D9 fails, also click "Report data issue" and do not copy the content.
If a sentence has two actions (joined by "and" or ";"), make two rows. Owner role = the owner of the linked BKB policy in the BKB-POL-000 index.
Full = a BKB policy clause AND a procedure AND an Annex A control exist. Partial = only one or two of the three exist. None = none exists.
Write: "Missing: <policy clause / procedure / control>. Owner: <policy owner>."

Covered = a clause has the same action AND the same time limit. Partly = the action is there but the time limit or owner is missing. Not covered = no clause. Where to fix: requirement names a country or office → Addendum; otherwise → Group policy. Redline frame: "<Role> shall <action> within <time limit>." Never make a Group value weaker; if it would, write "Exception needed".

Use the six fixed steps: 1 Trigger received → 2 Check input → 3 Do the action → 4 Record → 5 Tell the owner → 6 Exception: escalate. For each step copy the responsible role and the time limit from the addendum Section 5 or the policy clause shown on your task page. Do not invent numbers.

Look up the control frequency in Ref-Sampling and copy the minimum sample. Select the sample with the random seed shown on your task page (the platform does the selection when you click "Select sample").
Fieldwork starts 30 days after the end of the audit period. Due date = fieldwork start − 5 working days.
Copy for every request: "The evidence must be dated, show who produced it, cover the whole period and be an unchanged system export."
A control has a gap when it has fewer than 2 accepted files. For each gap write: "Please send 2 more files for <control> covering <period> by <due date>."

Effective: no exceptions. Effective with exceptions: only Low/Medium exceptions and ≤ 5 % of the population. Not effective: any High exception or > 5 %. Control tests (T8.2): 1–2 deviations = effective with exceptions; > 2 = not effective.
Copy the action for the exception type from Ref-Actions (e.g., U1 active leaver account → "Disable within 1 working day; check for use after termination" — owner IAM team).
Voluntary leaver: account disabled within 4 hours of termination. Involuntary leaver: within 1 hour. KPI = leavers fully disabled within SLA ÷ all leavers × 100.
One change-log row for each changed field: row ID, field, old value, new value, event ID, evidence.

Sort by residual score (highest first); for equal scores, higher inherent score first. Trend: score went up ↑, down ↓, no change →. "So what" frame: "If this happens, <consequence copied from the statement>." Risk for acceptance = the Medium risk with the highest residual score (equal scores: lowest Risk ID). Expiry = today + 12 months; re-assessment = expiry − 30 days; approver = rule R36.

Class 1: KEV-listed or Critical on an internet-facing asset → 7 days. Class 2: Critical, or KEV on an internal asset → 14 days. Class 3: High → 30 days. Class 4: Medium → 90 days. Due = first detected + SLA. Exception valid only if approved by system owner AND CISO, has a compensating control, and has not expired.
Write three recommendations: the Ref-Actions action for the three classes (or deviation types) with the most breaches, in that order.
High = affects a Mission Critical system or no evidence exists. Medium = done late or partly. Low = record-keeping only.

Use the tier from rule R35. Then include every question in Ref-Questions marked for that tier or a lower tier. Clause checklist: include every clause marked for the tier; add "transfer mechanism" if data leaves the country.

Check S1–S9 (Ref-SOC checks). Reject if S4 (qualified opinion) or S9 (service not in scope). Otherwise Approve with conditions if any S-check fails (one condition per failed check from Ref-Conditions, due in 90 days). Approve if none fails.

Role = the value in the dataset column "Role (contract register)". DPIA required = Yes if the activity involves any of: children or students, AI/analytics/profiling, monitoring or recording, health data, identity checks (KYC/AML). Otherwise No.

For every affected office and every data-subject country, look up the regimes in addendum Section 2. Deadline = discovery time (UTC) + clock. Mark the earliest firm deadline. Tell data subjects = Yes if the data includes children's data, health data, financial data or credentials, or more than 1,000 people; otherwise No.

Use the 4-week template: Week 1 lesson, Week 2 poster + quiz, Week 3 phishing simulation, Week 4 results + refresher. Copy the scenario card and the 3 behaviours for your theme from Ref-Content. Approvals: HR + Legal always; add works council where addendum Section 2 lists one for the office.

Copy the obligations from the official source (steps in T11.2). Applicability per office: rule R02. Affected policies: use the keyword table in Ref-Keywords. Action due date = publication date + 30 days.

An action is "Closed — verified" only if all are true: closure evidence is attached (else K1); it is dated after the action was raised (else K2); it is a system record, not a statement (else K3); the re-test passed (else K4). Otherwise the status is "Open" with the failed code. An open action more than 14 days past its due date and not yet escalated → escalate to the owner's manager (K5). Next check date = test date + 14 days.

Answer each request with ONE evidence file: same control or clause, dated inside the audit period, from a system (not an undated screenshot). Record file ID and SHA-256. If no file matches, answer "No evidence available" and raise an action (never create evidence after the request). For a finding: open the named evidence file — if it shows the problem, accept and state the corrective action; if it shows the control worked, challenge with the row; if still disputed, name the route (closing meeting, then the certification body's appeal process).

Critical: access to Tier 4 data or children's data at scale, OR a customer-facing or regulatory-critical service that is hard to replace. High: access to Tier 3 personal/confidential data at volume, OR a revenue-critical service. Medium: limited personal data or pseudonymous data, easy to replace. Low: only public/anonymous data. Check from Critical down; stop at the first match.

F1.1: What will I do
Your first day in the Group GRC Office. Complete onboarding: record your assignment, sign the undertaking and data rules, and submit your completed READ-ME-FIRST file.
Why am I doing this

Every GRC job starts with conduct: you handle other people's data and you produce records that auditors rely on. Before you touch any task, the organisation needs proof that you know the rules (BKB-POL-024 Section 6.1) and that your workspace records your work correctly.
What will I learn
Follow the mentee conduct and data rules — synthetic data only, own work, no AI tools for task work — see BKB-POL-024 Section 3.1; BKB-POL-022 Section 7.1

Clause 6.2 requires measurable information security objectives; clause 6.1.1 the risks and opportunities of the ISMS itself; clause 7.1 the resources. The gap analysis turns 12 weeks of work into a 6-month implementation plan.

principles: G1
Half instructions, half decisions
About 50 % of every task's activities are decisions made from options provided; the rest are numbered instruction steps. Each task shows its judgement share.
G2
Decisions use provided options
The mentee never writes an opinion from nothing: each decision offers fixed options (A/B/C, or a drop-down per row). The rules in Ref-Rules tell the mentee how to choose.
G3
Feedback after every decision
After submission the mentee sees the best option and a one-line reason. Wrong choices are learning points, not penalties beyond the scoring weight.
G4
Fixed templates and sentence frames
Outputs are templates with drop-down lists. Where text is needed, the mentee completes a sentence frame. Free writing is not assessed.
G5
Plain English
Short sentences, common words, one action per step (CEFR level B1). A glossary explains every GRC term. English style is never scored.
G9
Foundation weeks: less is more

Weeks 1–2 teach one rule per task with a worked example before every decision type: no risk assessment, no Lead Implementer extension, at most six steps and three decisions per task, at most eight hours per week, one scripted message per task.
G6
Task messages carry a learning point

Each task sends scripted messages (one in the Foundation weeks, two from week 3): a situation to decide (A/B/C) and either an extra data file or a data-handling decision. Each ends with why it matters.
G7
Help is scripted, never a chat

There is no agent or person to chat with. Every step carries a pre-written help note (?) and names its rule; the Learn section holds the glossary and the rule tables; "Report a problem" is a form answered by the programme office. Nothing on the platform gives the answer to a decision.
G8
Reviews check decisions and evidence
AI and human reviewers score decision accuracy against the key, correct rule application, evidence for every row, and data handling.

principles: One workspace per mentee on the GRCMentorship platform, provisioned at onboarding (BKB-POL-024 Section 6.1 step 3). Nothing is submitted by e-mail or chat.
Everything the mentee does is captured as a record: artefacts, a structured work log, an evidence trail, task-message responses and problem reports.

Synthetic data only: every dataset is generated by the assignment engine; mentees never handle live, production or real personal data (BKB-POL-024 Section 3.1; BKB-STD-001 handling matrix "Mentee use").
Records are immutable once submitted: each submission gets a SHA-256 hash, a UTC timestamp and a version number; resubmission creates a new version and never overwrites.
Evidence-quality rules that mentees learn in Week 2 (BKB-POL-016 Section 7.1: dated, attributable, complete for the period, unaltered) apply to their own work.
The mentee ticks each instruction step, records each decision (option chosen) and the rule used; the platform records the rest automatically.
folders: Undertaking, privacy-notice acknowledgement, data and AI rules acknowledgement
Read-only: dataset(s), instructions and the library task anchor issued by the engine
Drafts and scratch files (not assessed; retained for integrity checks)
Task messages received and the steps ticked (INJECT_LOG)
Automated review record, assessor review record, moderation and re-check records (read-only to mentee)
Knowledge checks, Foundation Gate Exam, Final Exam forms and results
Auto-compiled portfolio of all submitted work and final transcript
worklog: Step number — set when the mentee ticks the step as done
The step text (copied by the platform)
For decision steps: option chosen (A/B/C or per-row value) — compared with the key after submission
Rule ID used in the step (R01–R36, L01–L25) or "copy" / "calculation"
Document and section or dataset row ID used (e.g., BKB-POL-006 Section 6.2; UAR row U-0142)
Yes/No — the scripted help note (?) was opened for this step (never penalised)
Minutes between step start and tick
Link to a "Report a problem" form sent from this step, if any
capture.evidence_trail: Every finding, rating or mapping in a submission must cite the dataset row ID(s) or document clause it rests on in a column named "Evidence ref". The automated review rejects findings without an evidence reference.
capture.retention: Mentee records are retained for 3 years after programme completion under a dedicated privacy notice (BKB-POL-024 Section 3.1), then deleted.
late: Due dates are set by the system; the deadline is 23:59 on the due day (mentee's time zone).
Late submission: −10 % of the task score per started 24 hours, for up to 72 hours; after 72 hours the task scores 0 but must still be submitted to count towards completion.
One grace period per programme: the system automatically applies a 48-hour extension without penalty to the first late task.
Task messages are answered within 2 working days and scored 0–4 on the task-message rubric.
Moderation: when the AI and human scores for the same deliverable differ by more than 15 points, a Moderator third-marks it blind; the moderated score replaces both (BKB-POL-024 Section 6.2 step 3).

Re-checks are automatic: every task scored below 65 and every final result below Pass is re-checked by a Moderator before it is released; no action is needed from the mentee. A mentee may still ask for a re-check with the "Request re-check" form (a right, not a task).
schedule: The programme sets every due date (Home › My plan). The mentee does not enter, select or change working hours or dates.
The 12-Week Plan shows the planned task hours per week (about 6–8 hours in weeks 1–2, 12–16 hours from week 3). Only due dates and submitted work are checked.
Reminders and scripted task messages arrive in the platform inbox and stay there until the mentee opens them; nothing is sent outside the platform.
If the mentee records no activity for 7 calendar days, the programme office makes a welfare check.

items: Weekly knowledge checks: 10 questions, 15 minutes, open book, two attempts (new form each time).
Foundation Gate Exam at the end of week 2: 30 questions, 45 minutes, pass mark 70 % (one resit).
Performance tasks: the extracts you receive contain planted problems. The rules find them when you apply them step by step.
Decisions: about half of every task; scored against the answer key (best option per situation or per row).
Task messages: one per task in weeks 1–2, two per task from week 3; a situation to decide and an extra data file or data-handling decision.
Final Exam in week 12: 40 questions (60 min) plus a 30-minute practical — a 60-row access extract with 8 hidden exceptions.
gates: Foundation Gate Exam ≥ 70 % (one resit on a new form within 5 working days; a failed resit defers the mentee to the next cohort).
At least 22 of 25 tasks submitted (≥ 85 % — the Charter KPI for task completion).

No confirmed integrity breach (use of live/real data, copying another mentee's work, impersonation, or use of any AI tool for task work — the platform has no chat assistant; all help is scripted). A confirmed breach is an automatic fail and is reported to the Programme Quality Lead.

acrit: All required artefacts, fields and rows present; every numbered step ticked in the work log.
Accuracy and decisions against the answer key
Decision points: best option chosen (per scenario, per row for item decisions). Planted defects found, no false findings, calculations correct within tolerance.
Every finding has an evidence reference (row ID or clause); references are real and correctly cited.
Template unchanged, naming convention, manifest, steps ticked and rule IDs recorded.
Submitted by the system due date; task messages answered within 2 working days.
hcrit: Choices match the key; where a choice differs, the rule and evidence cited show a reasonable reading. Patterns of wrong choices become coaching points.
Every value has a source (document + section, or dataset row) in the "Evidence ref" column.
Instruction steps done; rules applied as written; templates and frames used as issued; task messages answered.
Accuracy and completeness of the record
Values copied exactly; calculations correct; no empty required field.
Only workspace data used; drills reported; own work; nothing sent outside the platform.
bands: and no composite below 75; digital badge "GRC 101 — Distinction"
remediation path: repeat up to 4 failed weeks in the next cohort with newly generated, unique tasks (once)

Meets the brief fully; minor issues only.
Mostly meets the brief; some material errors or gaps that a reviewer would send back.
Partially meets the brief; significant errors; needs close supervision.
Missing, wrong, or not the mentee's own work.
hc: Rules R04 and R05 applied correctly; facts copied accurately with a source for every value; decision-tree path recorded for every asset.

Rules R11–R13 applied correctly; look-ups complete; redlines follow the frame; fix location (Group or Addendum) correct. ISO/IEC 27001 LI extensions: LI-05 — L06/L07 applied exactly; every justification has a source. LI-06 — L08/L09 applied exactly.
Rules R09, R15 and R18–R20 applied correctly; test plan followed unchanged; every exception traceable to a dataset row.

Rules R06–R08, R19, R22 and R24–R26 applied correctly; numbers traceable; test script followed unchanged. ISO/IEC 27001 LI extensions: LI-09 — L12 applied correctly. LI-11 — L16 applied; formula reproduces the value. LI-12 — L17/L18 applied exactly.
Rules R28 and R30 applied correctly; every deadline traceable to an addendum row; legal sign-off box ticked. ISO/IEC 27001 LI extensions: LI-14 — L20 applied correctly.

Rules R33 and R34 applied correctly; closure decisions and escalations justified by the evidence; right evidence file for each auditor request; response to the finding follows the evidence. ISO/IEC 27001 LI extensions: LI-17 — L23/L24 applied correctly; readiness verdict follows the rule. LI-18 — clause quoted; response follows the evidence.
inject_format: Situation — one or two short sentences from the current task (plain English).
Options — A, B, C (DECISION and DRILL), or numbered steps for an extra data file (DATA).
Learning point — shown after answering: the best option and why it matters.
Read — the rule or document that guides the choice.
inject_rubric: DECISION/DRILL: best option chosen. DATA: rows added and rules applied correctly.
DECISION: a defensible but weaker option (named in the key). DATA: rows added with one error.
Answered late (after 2 working days) or DATA incomplete.
Not answered, wrong option, OR (DRILL) the offered data was accepted or forwarded.

human: Certified GRC professional (e.g., CISA, ISO/IEC 27001 Lead Auditor/Implementer, CRISC, CIPP/E/US/T, CISSP) with ≥ 5 years' GRC experience.
Scores Human Checkpoints HC1–HC6; gives written feed-forward; flags integrity concerns. Ratio 1 : 35 mentees.
Senior assessor who has passed calibration with ≥ 0.75 agreement for two consecutive months.
Third-marks any deliverable where AI and human scores differ by > 15 points; performs automatic re-checks of low scores.
Cybersecurity Program Manager (policy owner of BKB-POL-024) or delegate.
Runs monthly calibration, AI-reviewer assurance sampling, final re-checks and cohort reporting.
voice: every pre-written note gives one instruction at a time in simple English, says which rule applies and where the value is, and never gives the answer to a decision

threads: Who the organisation is, which laws and standards apply, and what changes when a regulator changes the rules.

programme.title: GRC 101 — GRC Intern Mentorship
